section: Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India 1977
title: 28 recorded a decline in the incidence of suicides were Jammu & Kashmir (75.5%), Manipur (54.5%), Sikkim (50.0%), Haryana (26.3%), Andhra Pradesh (25.4%), Rajasthan (16.7%), Gujarat (14.2%), Tamil Nadu (14.1%), Uttar Pradesh (13.8%), Maharashtra (13.6%), Tripura (9.9%), Madhya Pradesh (7.9%), Punjab (7.5%) and Meghalaya (4.8%). It is worth mentioning that Jammu & Kashmir registered maximum decline in suicide cases (75.5%) in 1977 over 1976 while the same had recorded maximum increase (2350.0%) in 1976 over 1975. The incidence of suicides for the Union Territories as a whole recorded an increase of 11.4 per cent in 1977 over 1976. Out of 9 Union Territories 5 recorded a decline and the remaining 4 recorded an increase. Lakshadweep recorded the maximum decline (100.0%) though the numerical decrease was by only one. Other 4 Union Territories which recorded decline were A. & N. Islands (55.0%), Arunachal Pradesh (37.5%), Chandigarh (4.8%) and Goa, Daman & Diu (3.9%). The maximum increase was registered by Mizoram (57.1%) followed by D. & N. Haveli (47.1%), Pondicherry (46.5%) and Delhi (2.1%).
